# 2 Chronicles Chapter 36 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** The people of the land took Josiah's son Jehoahaz and made him king in Jerusalem in his father's place.

**2** Jehoahaz was twenty-three when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem.

**3** The king of Egypt dethroned him in Jerusalem and imposed on the land a levy of 100 talents of silver and a talent of gold.

**4** The king of Egypt made Jehoahaz's brother Eliakim king over Judah and Jerusalem and changed his name to Jehoiakim. Neco took Jehoahaz and carried him off to Egypt.

**5** Jehoiakim was twenty-five when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. He did evil in the eyes of the LORD his God.

**6** Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon attacked him and bound him with bronze shackles to take him to Babylon.

**7** Nebuchadnezzar also took articles from the LORD's temple to Babylon and put them in his temple there.

**8** The other events of Jehoiakim's reign, the detestable things he did, and everything found against him are recorded in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. His son Jehoiachin succeeded him.

**9** Jehoiachin was eighteen when he became king, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He did evil in the LORD's eyes.

**10** In the spring, King Nebuchadnezzar sent for him and brought him to Babylon, along with the valuable articles from the LORD's temple. He made Jehoiachin's uncle Zedekiah king over Judah and Jerusalem.

**11** Zedekiah was twenty-one when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem.

**12** He did evil in the eyes of the LORD his God and did not humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet, who spoke the word of the LORD.

**13** He also rebelled against King Nebuchadnezzar, who had made him take an oath in God's name. He became stubborn and hardened his heart, refusing to turn to the LORD, the God of Israel.

**14** Furthermore, all the leaders of the priests and the people became more and more unfaithful, following all the detestable practices of the nations and defiling the LORD's temple, which He had consecrated in Jerusalem.

**15** The LORD, the God of their ancestors, sent word to them again and again through His messengers, because He had compassion on His people and on His dwelling place.

**16** But they mocked God's messengers, despised His words, and ridiculed His prophets until the LORD's wrath against His people was so great there was no longer any remedy.

**17** He brought the king of Babylon against them, who killed their young men with the sword in the sanctuary. He had no mercy on young men or young women, the elderly or the infirm. God gave them all into Nebuchadnezzar's hands.

**18** He carried off to Babylon all the articles from God's temple, large and small, the treasures of the LORD's temple, and the treasures of the king and his officials.

**19** They set fire to God's temple, tore down the wall of Jerusalem, burned all the palaces, and destroyed everything of value.

**20** He carried into exile to Babylon those who survived the sword, and they became servants to him and his successors until the kingdom of Persia came to power.

**21** The land enjoyed its sabbath rests — fulfilling the word of the LORD spoken through Jeremiah — lying desolate until the seventy years were complete.

**22** In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia — in order to fulfill the word of the LORD spoken through Jeremiah — the LORD stirred the heart of Cyrus king of Persia to issue a proclamation throughout his realm, both verbally and in writing:

**23** "This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: 'The LORD, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth, and He has appointed me to build a temple for Him at Jerusalem in Judah. Anyone among you who belongs to His people — may the LORD his God be with him, and let him go up.'"


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **36:15-16**: "He sent word again and again because He had compassion" — even at the end, God keeps trying. He doesn't give up on His people until they give Him absolutely no choice. The destruction of Jerusalem is not divine cruelty; it's divine last resort.

- **36:21**: The land gets its Sabbaths. The exile is reframed not as punishment alone but as ecological justice — the land resting from the burden of a people who refused to let it rest. Creation, too, has rights under God's law.

- **36:22-23**: The last word of 2 Chronicles — the last word of the entire Hebrew Bible in Jewish canonical order — is "let him go up." Go up. Return. Rebuild. The story of God and His people does not end in ashes. It ends with an open door.


— PNEUMA
